n: On February 9, 1843, Joseph taught how to tell true messengers from false. First, angels can be resurrected beings with physical bodies of flesh and bones.
Jesus himself showed this after his resurrection, inviting disciples to touch him.
Second, “spirits of just men made perfect”—righteous people who have died but not yet been resurrected—who share the same glory.

f.w: spirits of just men made perfect

n: A practical test: if a messenger claims to come from God, offer to shake his hand.

f.g: A simple, physical test of the messenger’s nature.

n: A resurrected angel will shake hands, and you will feel it.
A righteous spirit without a body will appear in his glory, since that is the only way he can appear.
He won’t shake hands, since that would be deceptive—implying he has a body. But he will still deliver his message.

f.w: contrary to the order of heaven for a just man to deceive
f.g: Honesty is part of heaven’s order; a righteous spirit won’t pretend.

n: If it is the devil pretending to be an angel of light, he will offer his hand, but you will feel nothing—exposing him.

f.w: the devil as an angel of light

n: These are three great “keys” to discern whether a heavenly visitation is from God.
